title: Runtime Anomaly Fusion Dashboard and Failure Synopsis
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a unified dashboard that fuses traces, metrics and log-derived signals into a concise failure synopsis per request path. The goal is to reduce noisy alerts and make it fast for oncall and SREs to identify whether an adverse user-facing outcome is caused by upstream overload, network timeouts, model-side errors (rejections, invalid outputs), or transport-level failures (HTTP/gRPC codes). This dashboard will be both an aggregation layer (trends, fingerprints) and a drilldown entry point that links to full tracehooks, sampled logs, and model response snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows top 10 request fingerprints by failure rate for the past 24h with filters for route, model, region, and customer tier
Each fingerprint includes a dominant failure class (timeout, overload, model_error, transport_error) with proportions displayed
Clickable fingerprint opens a timeline view that correlates metric spikes (latency, queue-length), trace spans, and representative logs within ±2 minutes
Integration with tracehook sampling: user can request full-span capture for a fingerprint and see the trace ID linked to trace collector UI
SLO impact widget calculates estimated error budget consumption per fingerprint and suggests the likely remediation owner (runtime, infra, model)
tasks: Define fingerprint schema combining route, model_version, seq_length_bucket, and failure_signature
Extend tracehook metadata to emit failure_reason and model_status_code fields
Create ETL job to join metrics, logs, and tracehook-enriched spans into an OLAP table for dashboarding
Design and implement frontend: fingerprint list, stacked failure composition bars, drilldown timeline canvas
Add alert rules that surface new high-entropy fingerprints (sudden rise in previously unseen failure composition)
Write playbook snippets for common fingerprints (e.g., client-side timeouts vs model rejection) and link to runbooks
notes: We intentionally separate 'transport error' (HTTP/gRPC codes) from 'model_error' (LLM rejection, invalid response, kernel OOM).
Fingerprinting must be stable across minor route name changes; include route_id and hash of canonical prompt template where available.
OLAP table TTL should be 90 days for long-term trend analysis, with 7-day hot window for fast UI queries.
We should consider sampling policy changes: if a fingerprint exceeds threshold, raise sample rate for both spans and logs for 1 hour.
